answer: Faking identity means buying new hardware, re-staking, and sustaining the thread for many epochs, so the attacker's cost scales linearly with each sock-puppet node while honest agents pay once. Each agent must stake a relic bound to its hardware root and a continuous thread of signed epoch proofs; a prism splits that history into verifiable shards peers can audit. From qwe0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
